title: Semester and Locker
premise: Tamsin Oyelaran runs an anonymous gossip account that has quietly become the voice of Ashgrove Prep, until the senior class's college essay prompt — 'Describe a moment you were not who you thought you were' — starts surfacing secrets she never posted, secrets only someone inside her life could know. As the account is hijacked and her closest friends become suspects, Tamsin must trace the leak to the person who taught her that power over other people's stories feels like belonging. In the end, exposed at the last game of the season, she deletes the account, owns her name publicly, and discovers that being known without a mask is the only belonging that doesn't corrupt.
about_author: Ivo Ashgrove is the pen name of a former boarding-school debate coach who spent six years watching teenagers curate themselves for admissions officers. They write from a converted garage in coastal Maine, where they keep a locked drawer of unsent apology letters.

chapters.title: The Prompt
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. English teacher Ms. Ferro assigns the college essay prompt, and Tamsin watches the room go still as classmates realize they'll have to be honest somewhere. That night, her anonymous account @ashgroveanon posts a devastatingly accurate rumor about the quarterback. Emotional beat: the thrill of omniscience masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Fine, Obviously
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She navigates lunch tables she secretly narrates online, trading on her invisibility while her best friend Priya begs her to apply to schools with actual coding programs. A post about Priya's scholarship nearly slips out. Emotional beat: the cost of being everyone's confessor and no one's friend.

chapters.title: Someone Else's Voice
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. @ashgroveanon posts something Tamsin didn't write — a cruel detail about her own lab partner, Dev, that only three people could know. She checks her passwords; nothing's breached. Emotional beat: first cold spike of fear beneath the control she thought she had.

chapters.title: Dev Reads It Aloud
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Humiliated in the cafeteria, Dev decides not to shrink but to investigate, mapping who knew what and when. He notices Tamsin flinch at the post's phrasing. Emotional beat: anger sharpening into purpose, and an unexpected alliance forming.

chapters.title: The Locker
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Someone leaves a printed screenshot of her very first anonymous post in her locker — dated two years ago, before anyone should have known it was hers. Emotional beat: the past arriving like a debt collector; power revealed as something she never owned.

chapters.title: Labels
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya confronts Tamsin about the account, hurt that their friendship ran through a filter. Tamsin lies badly. Emotional beat: betrayal from both directions — Priya's trust cracking, Tamsin's double life collapsing inward.

chapters.title: Essay Season
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Draft essays circulate in workshop, and each one contains a secret Tamsin recognizes — secrets she told no one but the account. Someone is feeding the prompt back at the school. Emotional beat: paranoia blooming; every kindness now reads as surveillance.

chapters.title: The Ghostwriter
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev traces posting times to the library's media lab and finds a deleted user profile with admin privileges: someone with keys to the whole system. Emotional beat: the hunt becoming personal as he realizes he's protecting Tamsin whether or not she deserves it.

chapters.title: What Power Feels Like
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Flashback chapter: how Tamsin built the account after being frozen out freshman year, how the first viral post made her feel seen for the first time. Emotional beat: sympathy earned — corruption shown as a slow, reasonable-seeming slide.

chapters.title: Homecoming Odds
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The anonymous account promises to reveal 'the biggest secret in Ashgrove history' before the final football game. Bets spread through the halls; students start confessing preemptively. Emotional beat: the community turning on itself, spectacle replacing trust.

chapters.title: Ms. Ferro's Office
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Ms. Ferro, who reads every draft, gently tells Tamsin her essay is 'a defense brief, not a story' — and reveals she knows more than she says. Emotional beat: an adult seeing through Tamsin without punishing her, which is somehow worse.

chapters.title: Suspects
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev and Tamsin build a suspect board: the student body president, a jealous editor, a tech-savvy sophomore. Each theory collapses. Tamsin realizes the leaker knows her writing rhythms better than anyone alive. Emotional beat: dread narrowing toward someone she loves.

chapters.title: The Confession Prompt
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The account begins posting fragments of Tamsin's own private essay drafts — the ones about her father's deportation and the year of silence after. Emotional beat: exposure of the true self beneath the mask; grief weaponized against her.

chapters.title: Priya's Choice
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya figures out who the ghostwriter is but hesitates, because exposing them will also burn Tamsin. She sits on the truth through a sleepless night. Emotional beat: loyalty versus honesty, and the discovery that protecting someone can be its own betrayal.

chapters.title: Last Practice
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The week of the final game, the school buzzes; the principal threatens to trace the account legally. Dev gives Tamsin an ultimatum: come forward or lose him. Emotional beat: pressure cresting; every relationship now priced in truth.

chapters.title: Who Taught You This
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin confronts the ghostwriter — her mentor figure from freshman year, the older student who showed her the account's first login and never let go of the keys. The confrontation is quiet, almost tender, and utterly damning. Emotional beat: the corrupting inheritance named out loud.

chapters.title: The Biggest Secret
chapters.summary: Ghostwriter's POV. Hours before the game, the final post goes live: everything, including proof that Tamsin Oyelaran is @ashgroveanon. The school's group chats ignite. Emotional beat: total collapse — the mask torn off in front of everyone at once.

chapters.title: Under the Lights
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At the last game, Tamsin walks into the stands instead of hiding, takes the mic at halftime, and tells the truth herself — the account, the harm, the hunger to matter. Emotional beat: the climax as reclamation; shame transmuted into authorship of her own story.

chapters.title: Aftermath Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Fallout spreads: friendships recalibrate, some permanently lost. Dev chooses to stay, not because Tamsin is innocent but because she chose the hard version of honesty. Emotional beat: forgiveness as a decision, not a feeling.

chapters.title: Deleted
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin deletes the account live in front of Priya, then writes a new college essay — the real one, about the moment she wasn't who she thought she was. Emotional beat: grief for the power she loved, and the first breath of a self without handles.

chapters.title: What Priya Kept
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya admits she sat on the truth for a day, and the two friends rebuild on terms that don't require confession booths. The ghostwriter transfers out quietly, unrepentant. Emotional beat: belonging rebuilt brick by brick, with load-bearing honesty.

chapters.title: Semester's End
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. On the last day of term, Ms. Ferro returns Tamsin's revised essay with one word: 'Finally.' Tamsin signs her real name to something public for the first time — a byline in the school paper about the account's rise and fall. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; identity chosen, not assigned.
